summary: This article explains how cooking shows the difference between physical changes, like melting and dissolving, and chemical changes, like cooking an egg, rising dough, and roasting coffee beans.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Kitchen Chemistry” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: about the shape, size, or form of something, not what it is made of
about how a material changes into a new material
a kind of material, like water, salt, or iron

challengeTerms.def: not able to be changed back to how it was
a material in foods like eggs, meat, and beans that helps the body grow
a substance, often sour, like lemon juice or vinegar

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a kitchen is a good place to learn science? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the difference between a physical change and a chemical change.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review physical, chemical, and substance, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use irreversible, protein, and acid in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
